The microstructure of PWA 1480 contains a fine dispersion of coherent, cuboidal γ' with an average size of 0.5 μm and a low lattice parameter mismatch of less than 0.2%.
Monotonic and cyclic tests were conducted on PWA 1480 from 20 to 1093°C at strain rates of 0.5 and 50%/minute.
At low temperatures, the material exhibited an orientation dependent CRSS, tension-compression asymmetry, and anisotropic strain hardening, which was correlated with the ease of cube cross-slip.
At high temperatures, the material was isotropic and deformed by homogeneous γ' by-pass.
The activation energy analysis revealed two distinct temperature regimes: low temperatures with a constant activation energy, and high temperatures with a diffusion-controlled activation energy.
The temperature at which the transition from low to high temperature behavior occurred was a function of strain rate, ranging from 815°C at 0.5%/min to 927°C at 50%/min.
The Copley-Kear model for shearing and the Brown-Ham model for climb-assisted by-pass were found to be physically relevant for the low and high temperature regimes, respectively.
The tension-compression asymmetry and orientation dependence of the CRSS were attributed to the stress-dependent rate of cube cross-slip, as described by the Pope-Ezz model.
The Walker-Jordan constitutive model was found to be capable of modeling all aspects of the material anisotropy in PWA 1480.
The temperature and strain rate boundaries for the Walker-Jordan model were proposed, along with guidelines for numerical experiments.
